headline_of_day: AI Trade Unravels: Stocks Post Longest Losing Streak Since 2023
dek: A week-long slide pushed the S&P 500 down 2% and the VIX above 30, as Anthropic's IPO failed to calm AI-trade jitters.
big_picture: US equities fell for a seventh straight session, their longest losing streak since 2023, as the unwinding AI trade spread from megacap tech into emerging markets, copper and crypto. The S&P 500 dropped 2.02% to 7175.83, the Nasdaq 100 fell 2.21% to 26517.05 and the Dow lost 2.19% to 49097.06, with breadth brutally negative at just 38 advancers against 463 decliners. Anthropic's record $81.3 billion IPO failed to lift broader sentiment, with shares down more than 10% on their second trading day even as they hold above the $83 offer price, while Nvidia extended its post-earnings slide to a sixth session and AMD fell sharply on a short-seller report. The VIX spiked 8.2% to 30.76 and investors rotated into short-dated Treasuries, with gold and bitcoin both falling alongside stocks rather than acting as traditional havens.
three_things: AI-trade unwind is now a seven-session losing streak, the longest since 2023
Anthropic's $81B IPO pop reversed; shares still above offer price but down double digits
Risk-off is broad: copper, emerging markets and bitcoin are sliding alongside equities
market_pulse: S&P 500 -2.02% to 7175.83, Nasdaq 100 -2.21% to 26517.05, Dow -2.19% to 49097.06, Russell 2000 -2.18% to 2655.11. Breadth deeply negative: 38 advancers vs 463 decliners. VIX +8.16% to 30.76. 10Y yield -1.39% to 4.98%. DXY -0.27% to 103.65. WTI crude -0.70% to $81.86. Gold -1.56% to $3569.44. Energy Minerals and Finance were relative sector outperformers; Health Services (-3.87%) and Non-Energy Minerals (-3.00%) led sector losses.

stories.headline: Global stocks extend losing streak to seven sessions as AI trade unwinds
stories.summary: World equities fell for a seventh consecutive session, the longest losing streak since 2023, as the AI trade continued to unwind despite Anthropic's blockbuster IPO. The S&P 500 is approaching correction territory and the Dow briefly dipped below 50,000, with Asian semiconductor stocks also sliding overnight. The rout has spread beyond megacap tech into emerging markets and commodities, pointing to a broader repricing of AI-related risk.

stories.headline: Anthropic shares slide below opening pop in second day of trading
stories.summary: Anthropic's stock fell more than 10% on its second trading day, extending a retreat from the record $81.3 billion IPO that priced at $83 and opened at $111.50 on its Nasdaq debut. Shares closed their first day at $97.17 and remain above the offer price, but the slide reflects broader AI-valuation jitters rather than company-specific news. Analysts at Melius and Needham have initiated coverage with price targets of $155 and $150 respectively.

stories.headline: Nvidia's post-earnings slide extends to a sixth straight session
stories.summary: Nvidia shares fell another 3.3% to around $142 on Friday, deepening a six-day decline that began even after last week's earnings beat topped estimates. NYU's Aswath Damodaran argues the stock is now roughly 30% below fair value and says he is waiting for a price near $140 to add to his position. Given Nvidia's outsized index weighting, the slide is a key drag on broader market benchmarks.

stories.headline: AMD tumbles after short seller ties firmware to blacklisted Chinese server maker
stories.summary: AMD shares fell as much as 11.2% intraday and closed down 7.7% at $489.19 Thursday after Hunterbrook Media reported that newer AMD firmware had been showing up at IEIT Systems, a Chinese server maker the US blacklisted in 2025; Hunterbrook's affiliated fund holds a short position in AMD. The stock fell a further 6% in Friday premarket trading, erasing much of a nearly 45% rally that had taken shares from $404.40 on November 5 to $585.30 on November 12. AMD has disputed the report, saying it misrepresents its business practices and relationships.

stories.headline: China's AI firms scramble as Nvidia chip access tightens
stories.summary: Chinese AI companies that built infrastructure around Nvidia chips are struggling to secure adequate supply as export restrictions bite, forcing a scramble for alternative compute sources. The squeeze illustrates how US export controls continue to reshape the competitive landscape for AI infrastructure in China.

stories.headline: Emerging-market stocks edge toward bear market on AI-led slide
stories.summary: A benchmark emerging-market equity index is nearing bear-market territory after seven straight days of declines, driven by the unwinding of the AI trade. The slide shows how the retreat from AI enthusiasm has spread well beyond US megacap tech into global risk assets.

stories.headline: Copper slumps to lowest since March as AI selloff spreads to metals
stories.summary: Copper prices fell to their lowest level since March as traders price in weaker industrial demand tied to the AI-sector slump. The move shows the risk-off mood triggered by the AI trade unwind is now hitting commodity markets as well as equities.

stories.headline: Third-party breach exposes JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard customer data
stories.summary: A breach at a shared third-party vendor exposed customer data linked to JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard, reviving concerns about supply-chain cybersecurity risk across financial services. The scope of affected customers and remediation timeline were still being assessed as of Thursday.

stories.headline: Short-dated Treasury yields post biggest drop since 2025 on haven demand
stories.summary: Two-year Treasury yields fell the most since 2025 as investors sought safety in short-dated government debt amid the equity selloff, putting short bonds on pace for their best week in over a year. The move reflects a broader shift into risk-off positioning as the AI-trade unwind weighs on equities.

stories.headline: South Korea and Japan stocks sink more than 4% in tech-led regional rout
stories.summary: The Kospi and Nikkei 225 both dropped over 4% as the US tech selloff spread to Asian markets, hitting semiconductor and AI-linked names especially hard. The overnight declines set a weak tone for US futures heading into Friday's session.

stories.headline: SpaceX completes $32 billion debt sale to fund AI chip access
stories.summary: SpaceX finalized a $32 billion debt deal to fund AI chip access, pricing at yields above 8%, a borrowing cost that could set a template for similarly expensive financing structures across the industry. The deal underscores investor caution around AI infrastructure financing even as demand for compute remains robust.

stories.headline: Bitcoin falls to five-month low as AI rout spreads to crypto
stories.summary: Bitcoin dropped as much as 3.8% to below $62,000, its lowest level since roughly July, as the broader AI-driven selloff spread into crypto markets. Gold also fell about 3%, suggesting the current stress is driving broad de-risking rather than a flight to traditional havens.
